Kevin / team —

Attached is a concise baseline rate card and an example commitment table (see attachment: cost_model_comparison.xlsx). High-level summary inlined below. Numbers are USD, hosted API public list:

- Text generation (per 1k prompt+completion tokens): $0.06 / 1k tokens
- Embeddings (per 1k tokens): $0.03 / 1k tokens
- Streaming surcharge: $0.005 / 1k tokens (applies when using low-latency streaming endpoints)
- Enterprise support / SLAs add-on: $1,250 / month (optional)

Commitment examples (monthly committed tokens, blended effective rate):
- Pilot (50M/mo commit): 10% discount -> effective $0.054 / 1k tokens
- Growth (200M/mo commit): 20% discount -> effective $0.048 / 1k tokens
- Scale (500M/mo commit): 30% discount + reserved capacity guarantee -> effective $0.042 / 1k tokens

Competitive notes vs requested vendors (brief):
- OpenAI: Typically competitive public list for standard models; they have volume discounts but limited reserved capacity options unless you move to dedicated contracts. Latency comparable; per-token cost often higher for chat-optimized models.
- Anthropic: Similar to OpenAI on list rates; focusing on safety/guardrails. If privacy/isolation is needed, Anthropic and Redwood both offer private deployment but Redwood has mature transition tooling (same API surface for hosted -> private).
- Together: Good open model economics at high scale; requires more engineering to match Redwood's out-of-the-box routing/kv-caching which reduces effective token consumption in chat flows.
- AWS: Highly variable (SageMaker endpoints vs Bedrock), often higher infrastructure cost when you need guaranteed latency; good fit when a client wants full cloud stack integration.

Notes on parity asks: if you want to match a specific public competitor rate, provide the invoice/quote and target effective rate. We can usually align with a commercial match for multi-quarter commits, subject to a minimal contract term and reserved capacity commitments.

Attachment: cost_model_comparison.xlsx (Excel, 78KB) — includes a modeled P&L for 50M/200M/500M monthly ramps, assumptions for caching and average tokens saved by prefix caching.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the sheet.

—Marcus

Kevin —

Quick summary on latency & reserved capacity:
- Best-effort hosted pool (no reservation): p50 ~ 120–160ms, p95 ~ 380–520ms for 1.5k-context chat (depends on concurrency).
- Reserved capacity pool (dedicated GPUs for your tenant): p50 ~ 60–90ms, p95 ~ 140–200ms.

Reserved pools also include KV/prefix caching pinned to your model instances, which reduces end-to-end latency on repeated prompt prefixes and reduces billable tokens in many chat flows. For pilot reserved slots during peak windows, we can set up a small reserved pool with an hourly reservation charge plus a credits buffer; Marcus will outline the commercials.
